title: B1-09 · The ḥāl: state during action

blocks.text: B1-09 · The ḥāl: state during action
Lesson overview

He arrived tired, he went out crying, they went in laughing, he left without saying anything, he uses adjectives, Gerundi and phrases with Arabic has only one construction for all these cases, the ḥāl ( ⁧الحَال⁩ , "the state"): a word to the indeterminate accusative ( ⁧وَصَلَ مُتْعَبًا⁩ ) or a sentence introduced by ⁧وَ⁩ ( ⁧خَرَجَتْ وَهِيَ تَبْكِي⁩ ). It is very common in stories, accounts and the chronicle, and its endings in -an are the key to figuring out who does what. Two weeks.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 113–114), plus the EGY track

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Grammar G49, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. recognize and use the ḥāl of a word, to the indeterminate accusative, granted with his • bearer ( ⁧صَاحِبُ الحَالِ⁩ );
2. distinguish the ḥāl from the adjective ( ⁧رَأَيْتُ الرَّجُلَ مُسْرِعًا⁩ / ⁧الرَّجُلَ المُسْرِعَ⁩ );
3. build the state phrase with ⁧وَ⁩ + pronoun, with direct imperfection and with ⁧وَقَدْ⁩ + perfect;
4. to express "without" with ⁧دُونَ أَنْ⁩ , ⁧بِدُونِ⁩ , ⁧بِلَا⁩ ;
5. use the most frequent adverbs ( ⁧مَعًا⁩ , ⁧جَمِيعًا⁩ , ⁧وَحْدَهُ⁩ , ⁧شَخْصِيًّا⁩ , ⁧مُبَاشَرَةً⁩ );
6. translating the ḥāl in English with the adjective, the gerund, the while, the word "con', the word "con', the word "without'.
Two-week plan.

blocks.text: 1. Dialogue 1 · The Feast of Karīm
Maria could not go to the party for the new house of Karīm (B1-07) and asks Luke how it went.

rows: ⁧مَارِيَا: كَيْفَ كَانَتْ حَفْلَةُ كَرِيم؟ آسِفَةٌ، لَمْ أَسْتَطِعْ أَنْ آتِيَ.⁩
Maria: How was the feast of Karīm? I'm sorry, I couldn't come.
⁧لُوكَا: كَانَتْ رَائِعَةً! وَصَلْتُ مُبَكِّرًا، فَوَجَدْتُ كَرِيم وَحْدَهُ فِي المَطْبَخِ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِلُ أَنْ يَطْبُخَ شَيْئًا.⁩
Luca: It was wonderful! I arrived early and found Karīm alone in the kitchen trying to cook something.

⁧لُوكَا: نَعَمْ! وَكَانَ خَائِفًا جِدًّا مِنَ النَّتِيجَةِ. ثُمَّ جَاءَتْ إِيلِينَا تَحْمِلُ كَعْكَةً كَبِيرَةً، وَدَخَلَ بَاوْلُو ضَاحِكًا، لِأَنَّهُ صَعِدَ الطَّوَابِقَ الخَمْسَةَ سَيْرًا عَلَى الأَقْدَامِ.⁩
Yes! And he was very afraid of the result. Then came Elena with a big cake, and entered Paul laughing, because she had climbed the five floors on foot.
⁧لُوكَا: مَا زَالَ مُعَطَّلًا! جَلَسْنَا جَمِيعًا عَلَى الشُّرْفَةِ نَأْكُلُ وَنَتَحَدَّثُ. وَفِي آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ خَرَجْنَا مَعًا وَنَحْنُ نُغَنِّي أَغَانِيَ عَرَبِيَّةً قَدِيمَةً.⁩
Again, it's broken! We all sat on the balcony eating and chatting. And at the end of the night, we went out singing old Arab songs together.
Did you sing?! And what did the neighbors say?
⁧نَزَلْنَا الدَّرَجَ بِسُرْعَةٍ دُونَ أَنْ نَنْظُرَ خَلْفَنَا!⁩ … ⁧لَا أَعْرِفُ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩
Luca: I don't know... we went down the stairs in a hurry without looking back!

blocks.text: ⁧أَنْتُمْ مَجَانِينُ!⁩ ( ⁧تَضْحَكُ⁩ ) ⁧مَارِيَا:⁩ You're crazy!

What to notice. Ḥāl of a word: ⁧مُبَكِّرًا⁩ (here adverb), ⁧وَحْدَهُ⁩ • alone • • alone • ⁧خَائِفًا⁩ (predicted by ⁧كَانَ⁩ , ḥāl!), ⁧ضَاحِكًا⁩ "Laughter' means: ⁧سَيْرًا عَلَى الأَقْدَامِ⁩ "Hiking' means: ⁧جَمِيعًا⁩ "All" is "all," ⁧مَعًا⁩ "Together" is the same. State Phrases: ⁧وَهُوَ يُحَاوِلُ⁩ • while looking for • • • • • • • • • • ⁧وَنَحْنُ نُغَنِّي⁩ "Singing" is a song. Direct imperfection after a verb of motion or position: ⁧جَاءَتْ⁩ … ⁧تَحْمِلُ⁩ She came in with the car. ⁧جَلَسْنَا⁩ … ⁧نَأْكُلُ⁩ We sat down and ate. ⁧دُونَ أَنْ نَنْظُرَ⁩ • without looking • • ⁧كَعْكَة⁩ Cake. ⁧أَغَانِيَ⁩ "Songs" (pl. of ⁧أُغْنِيَة⁩ , diptototo). ⁧مَجَانِينُ⁩ Crazy (pl. of ⁧مَجْنُون⁩ ).
2. What is the ḥāl
The ḥāl responds to the question ⁧كَيْفَ؟⁩ How? in what state? and describes the subject or object at the time when the action takes place .
⁧خَرَجَ وَهُوَ يَبْكِي.⁩ How did he get out? ⁧وَهُوَ يَبْكِي⁩ the subject ⁧خَرَجَ⁩

The ḥāl is an extra element: if you remove it, the sentence remains complete ( ⁧وَصَلَ الوَفْدُ⁩ ). This distinguishes him from the predicate of ⁧كَانَ⁩ and similar verbs ( ⁧كَانَ خَائِفًا⁩ "He was frightened" where the accusative is mandatory.
3. The ḥāl of a word
Form: Indeterminate accusative . Agreement: gender and bearer number. The ḥāl is almost always a participle or an adjective.

rows: The two students came back happy.

blocks.text: The healthy male plural takes ⁧ـِينَ⁩ : ⁧دَخَلُوا ضَاحِكِينَ⁩ They came in laughing. The healthy female plural takes ⁧ـَاتٍ⁩ (with kasra, not the fatha). The diptotes as ⁧سُعَدَاءُ⁩ They only take one fatha: ⁧سُعَدَاءَ⁩ . Position. Usually after the verb and subject; may also be immediately after the verb, before the subject: ⁧وَصَلَ مُتَأَخِّرًا الوَفْدُ⁩ (journalistic style).
4. Ḥāl or adjective?
The same participle may be ḥāl or adjective: the determination decides it.
⁧رَأَيْتُ رَجُلًا مُسْرِعًا.⁩ adjective (undefined name) I saw a hasty man.
The rule of thumb. An indeterminate accusatory following a given name and responding to "how?" is a ḥāl. With an indefinite name the same form is usually an adjective.
5. Dialogue 2 · The award evening
Laylā tells Luca about the final evening of the Beirut festival.

rows: ⁧لُوكَا: لَيْلَى! شَاهَدْتُ حَفْلَ الخِتَامِ عَلَى الإِنْتَرْنِت. هَلْ فَازَ الفِيلْمُ المِصْرِيُّ؟⁩
Luca: Laylā! I saw the internet closing night. Did the Egyptian movie win?
⁧لَيْلَى: فَازَ بِالجَائِزَةِ الأُولَى! صَعِدَتِ المُخْرِجَةُ إِلَى المِنَصَّةِ وَهِيَ تَبْكِي مِنَ الفَرَحِ.⁩
Laylā: He won the first prize! The director went on stage crying with joy.

blocks.text: ⁧رَأَيْتُهَا! وَوَقَفَ الجُمْهُورُ مُصَفِّقًا دَقَائِقَ طَوِيلَةً.⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ I saw her! And the audience stood and applauded for long minutes.

rows: ⁧لَيْلَى: وَأَنَا كُنْتُ جَالِسَةً فِي الصَّفِّ الأَوَّلِ أَكْتُبُ بِسُرْعَةٍ. ثُمَّ تَكَلَّمَتِ المُخْرِجَةُ هَادِئَةً، وَشَكَرَتْ فَرِيقَهَا وَاحِدًا وَاحِدًا.⁩
Laylā: And I was sitting in the front row writing fast. Then the director spoke calmly and thanked her team one by one.
And you met her in person?
⁧لَيْلَى: نَعَمْ، بَعْدَ الحَفْلِ. جَاءَتْ إِلَيَّ مُبْتَسِمَةً وَقَالَتْ إِنَّهَا تَعْرِفُ تَقَارِيرِي! خَرَجْتُ مِنَ القَاعَةِ وَأَنَا لَا أُصَدِّقُ.⁩
Laylā: Yes, after the evening. She came to me smiling and told me she knows my services! I walked out of the room and couldn't believe it.
Laylā: Tomorrow I return to Beirut tired... but happy!

blocks.text: What to notice. ⁧وَهِيَ تَبْكِي⁩ "Crying" (state phrase with the pronoun). ⁧مُصَفِّقًا⁩ Claping (participle of form II as ḥāl). ⁧جَالِسَةً⁩ is preached by ⁧كُنْتُ⁩ ; ⁧أَكْتُبُ⁩ is an imperfect with value of ḥāl. ⁧هَادِئَةً⁩ • calmly (Lett. "calma": Italian often prefers a fashion complement. ⁧شَخْصِيًّا⁩ In person: ... ⁧مُبْتَسِمَةً⁩ Smiling, smiling. ⁧وَأَنَا لَا أُصَدِّقُ⁩ • without believing it (Lett. I don't think so. ⁧مُتْعَبَةً⁩ … ⁧سَعِيدَةً⁩ : two ḥāl Coordinate. ⁧حَفْلُ الخِتَامِ⁩ The closing evening is closed. ⁧الفَرَح⁩ "Joy" is the word. ⁧وَاحِدًا وَاحِدًا⁩ One by one.
6. The state phrase
The ḥāl can be an entire sentence ( ⁧الجُمْلَةُ الحَالِيَّةُ⁩ ). Three buildings:

rows: She came out crying. · He entered with a book in his hand.
imperfect without ⁧وَ⁩ (after verbs of motion and position)
He came running. · They sat and waited.

blocks.text: ⁧وَقَدْ⁩ + perfect (action already accomplished) ⁧عَادَ إِلَى قَرْيَتِهِ وَقَدْ تَغَيَّرَ كُلُّ⁩ He went back to his village, where everything had changed.

The ⁧و⁩ State ⁧وَاوُ الحَالِ⁩ ) does not mean "and": introduces the circumstance. It translates with ... ..while, with the gerund, with ... or with a relative, never with ... and... The pronoun refers to the bearer of ḥāl: ⁧خَرَجَ وَهُوَ⁩ …, ⁧خَرَجَتْ وَهِيَ⁩ …, ⁧خَرَجُوا وَهُمْ⁩ …. With the first person:
⁧خَرَجْتُ وَأَنَا⁩ …, ⁧خَرَجْنَا وَنَحْنُ⁩ ….
⁧وَقَدْ⁩ + perfect indicates a situation already achieved at the time of the main action: ⁧وَصَلْنَا وَقَدْ بَدَأَ الفِيلْمُ⁩ When we arrived, the film had already begun.
7. Without it
⁧دُونَ أَنْ⁩ / ⁧مِنْ دُونِ أَنْ⁩ + ⁧خَرَجَ دُونَ أَنْ يَقُولَ شَيْئًا.⁩ He came out without saying anything. conjunctive

rows: He left without a passport. · He entered without asking permission.
He went out without knowing the way.

blocks.text: 8. Fashion adverbs
Many expressions of fashion in -an are, grammatically, of ḥāl or similar constructions. Learn them as blocks:
⁧مُتَأَخِّرًا⁩ · ⁧مُبَكِّرًا⁩ early · late ⁧وَصَلَ مُتَأَخِّرًا.⁩
⁧وَحْدَ⁩ + pronoun agrees with the bearer: ⁧أَعِيشُ وَحْدِي⁩ , ⁧تَعِيشُ وَحْدَهَا⁩ , ⁧يَعِيشُونَ وَحْدَهُمْ.⁩
9. Translate the ḥāl

rows: ⁧خَرَجَ وَهُوَ يَتَكَلَّمُ⁩ → came out speaking / while talking
⁧دَخَلَ وَفِي يَدِهِ كِتَابٌ⁩ → entered with a book in hand
⁧وَصَلْنَا وَقَدْ بَدَأَ⁩ → we arrived that had already begun

blocks.text: A good check: if in your translation it appears before a circumstance, you have probably mistranslated a ⁧و⁩ State.
10. Pronunciation

The final -an. In ḥāl desinence is part of the meaning: ḍāḥikan, mubtasiman, mutʿaban. In pausing reading the last word of the sentence is read with -ā (wa-ṣala mutaʾaḫḫirā), but within the sentence pronunciation -an. The ⁧و⁩ State. wa-huwa yabkī, wa-hiya taḍḥaku: ⁧و⁩ binds to the pronoun without pause; a little break goes before the ⁧و⁩ , as a comma.
11. New lexicon
★ ⁧نَائِم⁩ nāʾim Sleeping ⁧ن و م⁩ active participle
★ ⁧فَرَح⁩ faraḥ joy ⁧ف ر ح⁩ name m. · ⁧مِنَ الفَرَحِ⁩ Joyful

Notes of use. ⁧نَظَرَ إِلَى⁩ is "look" (voluntary action); ⁧رَأَى⁩ is see. ⁧حَمَلَ⁩ it is carrying something in your hand or on you; to bring (with you) something to someone is used ⁧أَحْضَرَ⁩ ( B1-04). ⁧وَحِيد⁩ is only, without company or sole ( ⁧اِبْنُهُ الوَحِيدُ⁩ "His only child" is his/her only child. ⁧وَحْدَهُ⁩ is only "by" in the sense of "without other" as an adverb.
12. Examples in context

rows: The manager got mad at the meeting.
We found the sleeping baby on the couch.
She came in with a letter in her hand.
He left without paying the bill.
waṣalnā ilā l-maḥaṭṭati wa-qad ġādara l-qiṭār.
When we arrived at the station, the train had already left.

14. Reading
Reading 1 · The next place (partly vocalized)
Short story invented.
⁧المقعد المجاور⁩
⁧دخل الشابّ المقهى مُسْرِعًا، وجلس قرب النافذة وهو ينظر إلى ساعته. كان المقهى شبه فارغ في ذلك⁩
⁧الصباح: رجل عجوز يقرأ الجريدة وَحْدَهُ، ونادل يمسح الطاولات صَامِتًا.⁩
: ⁧أجاب الشابّ مُتَرَدِّدًا⁩ « ⁧تنتظر أحدًا؟⁩ » ⁧بعد دقائق، رفع العجوز عينيه ونظر إلى الشابّ مُبْتَسِمًا، ثمّ سأله:⁩
⁧وهي الآن التاسعة والنصف. لا تقلق يا بُنَيّ،⁩ » ⁧ضحك العجوز وقال:⁩ .« ⁧صديقة. كان موعدنا في التاسعة⁩ … ⁧نعم⁩ »
.« ⁧الانتظار جزء من الحبّ بقي الشابّ جالسًا لا يتكلّم، والعجوز يقلّب صفحات جريدته بهدوء. وفجأة انفتح الباب، ودخلت فتاة تحمل⁩
⁧وقف الشابّ مُنْدَهِشًا، فالورد كان من⁩ « ⁧آسفة! الحافلة تأخّرت كالعادة!⁩ » ⁧باقة من الورد وهي تضحك:⁩
